Traffic.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.2 binary, which carries full C++ symbols; the plugin publishes no source and the maker's site carries no manual for it. Traffic, Water and Hotel are one piece of hardware with three overlays, and the VCV plugin builds them as three models sharing a panel layout: three jacks across the top, a three-by-three knob grid, a three-way Mode switch, a two-way Voltage Range switch, three CV outputs and a pulse output. The knobs are all configured 0 to 1 with a default of 0, and the scaling is the same in all three models: value times 8 on the Unipolar setting, value times 16 minus 8 on Bipolar, so the CV outputs span 0 to 8V or -8V to +8V rather than the usual 10. Traffic's three trigger inputs are the only ones in the plugin that test against 0.3V; Water's and Hotel's test against 1V. The Mode switch's three choices are configured as Groove, ?? and Base at values 0, 1 and 2; the panel prints Base at the top of the toggle, ?? at the middle and Groove at the bottom, which matches a toggle whose lowest position is value 0. In the ?? mode the module fills three sixteen-entry tables with three-bit random numbers and reads the knobs through them; the exact stepping of those tables was not followed far enough to describe on a control's own line.

Water.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.2 binary. The three playheads are three separate eight-float vectors built from the same nine scaled knob values, each rotated to start at a different knob: A holds knobs one to eight, B holds knobs four to nine followed by one and two, and C holds knobs seven to nine followed by one to five (Water::process, 0xb6c0 to 0xb734). That is what the panel's Start A, Start B and Start C mark, and it is the three-phase reading the maker's one-line summary claims. Each output also carries a sixteen-entry table of indices, re-drawn with three-bit random numbers only on a rising edge at Rnd trig; the Mode switch, configured as All, Phase and Step at values 0, 1 and 2, selects how much of that table is re-drawn, and on All the step counters wrap at sixteen rather than at eight (0xbb64 onward). The panel prints Rnd above the switch and Step, Phase and All down its left side. The six knobs that are not a Start knob all carry the same line, because the module treats them identically. Knob values are scaled 0 to 8V on Unipolar and -8V to +8V on Bipolar.

Hotel.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.2 binary. The panel is the clearest of the three and it carries one plain error. Over the first knob of each row it prints 66% 3A and over the second 33% 3B, but the code draws a uniform number from 0 to 99 and takes the FIRST knob only when that number is above 65 (Hotel::process, 0x35b8), so the first knob is chosen about 34 per cent of the time and the second about 66. The draw was simulated against the module's own linear congruential generator to confirm the value is uniform over 0 to 99. The third knob of each row, printed Floor, is the voltage that output holds while the clock is low; in the Pool mode there is no floor at all and the output instead latches one of the row's three knobs picked at random, which is what the panel's Latch marking means. The Mode switch is configured as Pool, Bar and Disco at values 0, 1 and 2; the panel prints no names, only the three probability sets, and they match the code in that order: Pool 99, 75 and 40 per cent, Bar 33 per cent for all three rows, Disco 90, 69 and 42. The fourth output, printed Doorman 2%, fires on a separate xorshift generator whose value falls below 1310 out of 65536, which is 2.0 per cent. Reset copies a stored counter back into the random seed and Rnd trig advances that counter, which is how the maker's loopable random gates work. The output named 1A or 2B in configOutput is printed 1A or 1B on the panel. Knob values are scaled 0 to 8V on Unipolar and -8V to +8V on Bipolar.
